sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: International Brokerage of Ginned Raw Cotton and Synthetic Yarns

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid — Quebec applies civilian private law (Civil Code of Quebec) for partnership, contract, property and enterprise-registry matters, while federal public and criminal law follows the common law tradition; enterprise registration is governed by the Quebec civil-law statute, notably the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, RLRQ c. P-44.1.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between Canada and the People's Republic of China for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (FIPA), in force 1 October 2014 — applicable where PRC-resident partners or ultimate beneficial owners are present.

Convention Between Canada and the United States of America with Respect to Taxes on Income and on Capital (1980), as amended by the Fifth Protocol (2007) — applicable where US-resident limited partners are admitted.

Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the European Union, provisional application since 21 September 2017 — investment protection and trade facilitation for EU counterparties.
Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA), in force 1 July 2020 — governs tariff and trade rules for raw cotton bales exported from Canada to North American destinations.

Convention Abolishing the Requirement of Legalisation for Foreign Public Documents (Hague Apostille Convention), in force for Canada since 11 January 2024 — governs the authentication path for foreign corporate, identity and banking documents to be used in Quebec incorporation filings.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA) and regulations thereunder, including the Money Laundering (Proceeds of Crime) Regulations, SOR/2002-184; FINTRAC interpretative guidance for Trust and Company Service Providers (2024) applicable to the incorporating law firm and notary; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, RLRQ c. P-44.1, arts. 1-56 (name clearance, declaration of registration, beneficial-owner disclosure at arts. 30.1-30.10); Regulation respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, RLRQ c. P-44.1, r. 2; Civil Code of Quebec, arts. 2186-2258, specifically arts. 2235-2253 (société en commandite / limited partnership); Charter of the French Language, RLRQ c. C-11, arts. 51-51.1 (naming and French-language public documents); Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17 and United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. U-2 (sanctions enabling statutes).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — the public enterprise extract discloses the name and address of the general partner and the number and classes of limited partners, while the statutory beneficial-owner declaration (véritable bénéficiaire) filed under art. 30.1 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises is not public and is communicated only to designated authorities such as the police, tax administration, FINTRAC, AMF and other regulators upon lawful request.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Corporate Existence / Certificate of Good Standing of the corporate general partner (certificat d'existence légale / certificate of incumbency)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of the home jurisdiction of the general partner (e.g., Delaware Division of Corporations, Companies House, or comparable competent registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the source country (Canada's accession effective 11 January 2024); consular legalization required only if the source jurisdiction is not a party to the Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (procuration / pouvoir) granted by the corporate general partner to the Quebec resident representative for signing the Declaration of Registration, name-reservation instruments and ancillary filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the general partner's home jurisdiction, including notarial certificate and signature verification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille on the notarial certificate; where the source state is not an Apostille party, double consular legalization through Global Affairs Canada and the foreign consulate in Canada

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true passport copies and proof of residential address for each natural-person ultimate beneficial owner, signatory, director and officer of the general partner (AML/CFT identification package)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent public authority of the document's source country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille on the notarial certification sheet; certified French or English translation annexed

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds attestation covering the initial capital contribution to the limited partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Funding financial institution of the general partner (correspondent or home bank maintaining the account)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille on the bank officer's attestation or notarized acknowledgement of the bank's signature; acceptable as part of KYC file for the SWIFT LC and documentary-collection payment rails

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration certificate (attestation de bénéficiaire effectif) executed by the general partner and each ultimate beneficial owner, annexed to the notarial limited partnership contract
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Quebec notary (notaire en pratique) at signature of the contrat de société en commandite
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Not applicable — instrument executed in Quebec and authenticated en minute before a Quebec notary; no apostille required for the Quebec-origin act, although underlying foreign evidence must carry apostilles

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory client-acceptance screening against (i) the consolidated Canadian sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA) and the United Nations Act; (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) FATF high-risk and non-cooperative jurisdictions statements; (iv) domestic, foreign and international-organization politically exposed persons (PEPs) under PCMLTFA regulations, with enhanced due diligence whenever a PEP holds 10% or more of the partnership or controls the general partner; (v) the RCMP criminal record screening where senior management or UBO history indicates integrity risk. Screening against the US OFAC SDN list is not statutorily required for a non-regulated trader but is contractually required by Canadian banks for USD-denominated SWIFT letters of credit and documentary collections supporting the raw cotton bales export flows. All hits, near-hits and escalated matters are documented in the client-acceptance memorandum retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online services portal at rgq.services (Services en ligne) for name reservation; public search facility accessible via the Registre des entreprises du Québec public extract service (registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca); filings may also be submitted in person at REQ service points in Quebec City and Montreal.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (RLRQ c. C-11), art. 51, the enterprise name must be in French; a name in a language other than French is permitted only where the registration also contains a French version and the enterprise uses the French version in Quebec. Each admissible name must contain (a) a distinctive element, (b) an optional descriptive element, and (c) a legal-form element in French, being 'société en commandite' or the abbreviation S.E.C.; the English variants 'Limited Partnership' or L.P. are recognized where a French version is co-registered. Non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters with French diacritics; alphanumeric and numeric distinctives are admissible. The REQ Name Guidelines (Directives relatives aux noms d'entreprise) prohibit names that are misleading, contrary to public order, or likely to interfere with third-party rights, and require prior ministerial or regulatory consent for all reserved and sensitive tokens.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque, Bank, Caisse, Trust, Fiducie — reserved for licensed financial institutions under the Bank Act and provincial deposit-institution statutes
Assurance, Insurance, Mutuelle — reserved for licensed insurers
Université, Collège, École, Institute — require prior approval of the competent educational ministry when used in an educational context
Royal, Royale, Reine, Queen, Crown, Impérial, Government, Public — imply Crown or governmental patronage and require federal or provincial consent
Canada, Québec, Montréal, Ville de, Province de — geographic or public-authority terms capable of creating confusion; require justification and may be refused
Bourse, Stock Exchange, Marché — imply a securities exchange and require AMF (Autorité des marchés financiers) authorization
Coopérative, Coop, Mutuel — reserved for recognized cooperatives and mutual companies

S.E.C., Société en commandite, Limited Partnership, L.P. — legal-form indicators restricted to registered limited partnerships; the tokens Inc., Ltée, S.A., Corporation and Corp. are prohibited for this vehicle type

Misleading, obscene, defamatory or public-order-contravening expressions, and names of designated terrorists or sanctions-listed entities — refused automatically by the Registrar under art. 16 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The base name reservation is valid for 90 days under art. 19 of RLRQ c. P-44.1; an extended reservation up to 12 months is available under art. 20 where the name is intended for a notarial instrument or declaration of registration not yet executed, upon filing the appropriate justification with the REQ. Upon refusal, the applicant or its mandatary may (1) request a review by the Registraire des entreprises within 30 days of the refusal, submitting legal arguments and any required ministerial or regulatory consents; (2) if the Registrar maintains the refusal, appeal de novo to the Court of Quebec within 30 days of the review decision, in the judicial district of the applicant's establishment or domicile. As a practical matter, the applicant may in parallel reserve an alternative distinct name to preserve deal timing for the cotton export contracts, and may re-file for the contested name after obtaining the required prior authorizations.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for an ISIC 4620 international brokerage entity with no retail or warehousing footprint in Quebec, subject to conditions: the registered establishment (siège social) must be a physical street address in Quebec at which documents can be served; a post-office box or disembodied mail drop is rejected by the REQ; a professional virtual-office operator providing dedicated meeting space, mail handling and service-of-process acceptance is acceptable. To preserve commercial substance under CRA GAAR and FINTRAC expectations, the LP should maintain at least one Quebec-resident compliance and booking officer, substantive board and partnership decisions taken in Quebec, the partnership ledger and minutes physically or electronically located in Quebec, and a Canadian bank account through which the documentary-collection and SWIFT LC transactions are settled.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate — estimated 5-10% probability of an unannounced on-site verification by the Registraire des entreprises within a three-year period for address-validity checks; approximately 15-25% probability that the Canada Revenue Agency will scrutinize the Quebec establishment and economic substance of the pass-through LP where brokerage commissions are routed to offshore limited partners; FINTRAC does not physically inspect non-reporting traders. Banks offering documentary-credit facilities typically rely on financial-data review and the KYC dossier rather than physical inspection.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Fee for reservation of enterprise name (réservation du nom) at the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under RLRQ c. P-44.1, r. 6 — CAD 25 per reservation, non-refundable upon rejection.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Fee for registration of the declaration of registration (déclaration d'immatriculation) of the société en commandite
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under RLRQ c. P-44.1, r. 6 — CAD 34 for the primary registration filing.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal fees for drafting the limited partnership agreement (contrat de société en commandite), UBO disclosure appendices, PEP and sanctions screening, client acceptance file, and coordination of all registry filings
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Qualified Quebec avocat and/or notary — private legal counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark — fixed professional quote of approximately CAD 2,500, reflecting 6-10 hours of senior professional time inclusive of AML file assembly.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial authentication of signatures of the general partner and limited partners on the declaration of registration and powers of attorney before a Quebec notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Chambre des notaires du Québec — notary of the partnership law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notarial tariff — approximately CAD 150 per attendance for authentication and related notarial formalities.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille certification fees in the home jurisdiction of the corporate general partner and ultimate beneficial owners (estimated for four instruments at approximately USD 40 each)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of the source country (e.g., U.S. Department of State, UK FCDO, or PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory or ministerial fee schedule of the issuing authority, variable between USD 15 and USD 75 per document depending on the source jurisdiction.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation into French of foreign-issued corporate incumbency, banking and identity documents, including sworn translator certification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translator member of OTTIAQ (Ordre des traducteurs, terminologues et interprètes agréés du Québec)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark — approximately CAD 165 flat fee per document set, or CAD 0.20-0.35 per source word for length-based quotation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered establishment (siège social) address in Montreal or Quebec City with service-of-process and mail handling — 12-month term
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered-office or virtual-office service provider (private sector)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark — approximately CAD 360 per annum for a qualifying physical street address and agent-for-service arrangement.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Quebec (CCQ), Book Four, arts. 2236-2262 (limited partnership or societe en commandite); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR, c. P-44.1), arts. 19-27 and 59-70 (declaration of registration and registers); Regulation respecting the tariff of fees payable to the Registraire des entreprises (CQLR, c. P-44.1, r. 2).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ), an autonomous registrar operating within Services Quebec, Ministere de l'Economie, de l'Innovation et de l'Energie.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration d'immatriculation (Registration Declaration) of a societe en commandite, filed electronically through the REQ online secure portal (Messagerie d'affaires).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow or blocked account is mandated for a Quebec limited partnership. Contributions, which may include in-kind cotton inventory or contract rights, are fixed in the partnership agreement and credited to partners' capital accounts as contractually agreed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WHEREAS [GENERAL PARTNER] has executed a Partnership Agreement with the Limited Partners, establishing [NAME] Limited Partnership (societe en commandite) under the Civil Code of Quebec; IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED: 1. The capital contributions set out in Schedule A are approved and credited to the partners' capital accounts, and the business of international brokerage of raw cotton and textile yarns is adopted. 2. The registered office of the Partnership is fixed at [ADDRESS, Quebec, Postal Code], and the Registrar is instructed accordingly. 3. [OFFICER] is appointed Managing Director with signing authority over bank accounts, trade documents and customs filings. 4. All costs incidental to formation, including registry and professional fees, are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name search, reservation and linguistic conformity check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) online name search and reservation service; Office quebecois de la langue francaise for French-name conformity.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the REQ database for identical or confusingly similar names, reserve the proposed name, and obtain the certificate of reservation. Ensure the partnership name is in French or has a French version and includes a legal element such as 'S.E.C.' or 'L.P.'.
required_dossiers: Proposed name in French (with optional English variant)
Statement of principal activity (ISIC 4620 / NAICS 424590)
Identification of the general partner requesting the reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a second or third choice or request formal administrative review by REQ under article 17 of the legal publicity regime; alternatively amend the name and re-file without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the partnership agreement (contrat de societe en commandite)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private legal instrument finalised by counsel, notary or partnership; no governmental pre-approval required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and sign the limited partnership agreement defining capital accounts, profit and loss sharing, the powers and mandate of the general partner, the limited partners' non-participation rule and voting rights, duration, and exit mechanisms. Notarization is required only if real property or in-kind registered assets are contributed; otherwise a private writing suffices.
required_dossiers: Identity documents or corporate excerpts of general and limited partners
Schedule of capital contributions (cash, receivable or cotton inventory)
Registered office address in Quebec
ISO/NAICS business description for the cotton bale export brokerage
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Defects in the agreement are cured by a supplementary instrument (avenant) or corrective resolutions; the executed version must be retained with the corporate records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of first governance resolution, registered office and signing mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General partner acting as governing organ of the limited partnership; internal corporate records.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the written resolution fixing the registered office in the Province of Quebec, appointing the managing director (or partnership manager) with signing authority for bank accounts, trade finance and customs documents, and ratifying pre-incorporation costs. Keep a book of resolutions and a register of partners.
required_dossiers: Consent to act of the general partner or corporate representative
Proof of physical registered office (lease or occupancy title in Quebec)
Original signed first resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the office address changes before registration, adopt an amending resolution and, after registration, file a declaration of modification with REQ within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the declaration of registration with the Registraire des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - online filing through the secure Messagerie d'affaires of Services Quebec.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the REQ transactional portal, select the declaration of registration for a 'societe en commandite', input the partnership name, head office address, activity code NAICS 424590, identity of the general partner, and the contributions of the limited partners. Attach the supporting files, pay the tariff, and download the certificate of registration (certificat d'immatriculation), which confers standing and a distinct patrimony on the limited partnership.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership agreement
Name reservation certificate issued by REQ
Identification of the general partner (individual ID or corporate excerpt)
Registered office address in Quebec
Total amount of limited partners' contributions
Statement of activities (ISIC 4620 / NAICS 424590, raw cotton bales export brokerage)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a notice of deficiency or refusal, file a corrective declaration within the prescribed period (generally 30 days). If rejected on the merits, request administrative review by the Registrar, then apply to the Court of Quebec for judicial review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and provincial tax registrations and customs account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Quebec; Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) for export programs.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the federal Business Number (BN) via the CRA Business Registration Online service; register for GST/HST (RT), payroll (RP) and, for QST purposes, with Revenu Quebec (TVQ account). Enrol the general partner as the responsible person, select the partnership fiscal year end, and apply for a CBSA client/account reference for export declarations where goods are shipped.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration issued by REQ
Partnership agreement with fiscal year election
Registered office address and postal address
Social insurance number or BN or corporate identification of the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Inconsistencies are corrected online through the CRA Business Account or Revenu Quebec's secure portal; voluntary disclosure to CRA/Revenu Quebec can waive penalties for inadvertent registration errors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal and occupational clearances (conditional on warehousing or premises)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal permit office (e.g., Ville de Quebec or Ville de Montreal) and municipal fire safety service; CNESST for workplace health and safety registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the partnership occupies premises for cotton bale storage or office space, obtain the municipal business permit (permis d'exploitation d'entreprise or equivalent), verify zoning conformity for a brokerage/storage occupancy, and schedule a fire safety inspection for baled cotton storage. Register as an employer with CNESST if personnel are engaged and subscribe to a workplace health and safety program.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration of the limited partnership
Lease or ownership title of the premises
Fire prevention compliance inspection request
Zoning and occupancy certificate application
CNESST employer registration form (if employees)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where municipal permits are refused, retain a professional (engineer/architect) to file compliance plans and, if needed, appeal to the municipality's permit review committee within 30 days; CNESST refusals are corrected by filing updated health and safety plan documentation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No provincial industrial manufacturing licence applies to a pure brokerage and commission trade in raw cotton bales (ISIC 4620 / NAICS 424590). If warehousing is added, the applicable authorities are the municipal permit office and the Ministere de l'Economie, de l'Innovation et de l'Energie (MEIE) for industrial policy guidance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required at federal or provincial level for the brokerage of raw cotton; a municipal business permit (permis d'exploitation d'entreprise) and, where premises are occupied, an occupancy certificate (certificat d'occupation) may be required by local by-law.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministere de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Registration only (Category C level of review). Pure commercial brokerage is not listed in the Regulation respecting environmental impact assessment and review (REAFIE), so no full EIA report is required. Any future storage depot project will be assessed on a registration basis depending on footprint, drainage and fire-water containment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No VOC or process wastewater is generated by brokerage. Applicable thresholds: municipal stormwater and solid waste by-laws for bale wrapping and straps; Quebec occupational exposure limits for cotton dust under the Regulation respecting occupational health and safety (RSST) during any handling or bale-opening; National Fire Code of Canada and Quebec Construction Code separation requirements for baled cotton storage; all waste removed by a permitted hauler.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety conformity certificate issued by the municipal fire safety service; structural load inspection certificate for racking or baled cotton storage; electrical installation conformity certificate issued by the Regie du batiment du Quebec (RBQ); CNESST workplace registration and health and safety program clearance where employees are engaged.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - federal income tax and GST/HST administration (portal: My Business Account, canada.ca/taxes); Revenu Quebec - Quebec Sales Tax (QST) and provincial tax administration (portal: Mon dossier d'entreprise, revenuquebec.ca); Registraire des entreprises du Quebec - limited partnership registration and NEQ issuance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the foreign/extra-provincial limited partnership with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec to obtain the NEQ (Numero d'entreprise du Quebec); a non-resident LP must appoint an attorney for service in Quebec. Step 2: Apply to the CRA for a federal Business Number (BN) with RC (income tax) and RT (GST/HST) accounts online or via Form RC1; the LP files annual T5013 partnership information returns. Step 3: Register with Revenu Quebec for QST within 30 days of beginning taxable activity in Quebec (Form LM-101-V); the QST account uses the NEQ with 'TQ' suffix. Step 4: Open a CBSA export-reporting sub-account (RM) under the BN to file Canadian Export Declarations via CERS. Step 5: Activate bank trade finance rails (SWIFT LC / documentary collection) and obtain inward remittance credit advices from the Canadian financial institution.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - A Quebec LP is fiscally transparent under the Income Tax Act (Division F) and the Quebec Taxation Act; income is allocated to partners pro rata and taxed at partner level; the LP files only information returns (T5013/Releve 16) and pays no entity-level income tax. For GST/HST and QST, however, the LP is a deemed person and registers separately. Limited partners are subject to at-risk rules that cap deductible losses at their at-risk amount.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (BoC); Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential regulation; Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for AML/EFT reporting
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates a fully liberalised capital and current account. The CAD is freely convertible and the repatriation of profits by non-resident limited partners is unrestricted, subject solely to federal Part XIII withholding tax on specified passive payments and applicable Bilateral Income Tax Treaty relief. No FX licensing or allocation is required for a Quebec export LP.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory requirement exists in Canada to convert or surrender export proceeds. An exporter may hold or disburse foreign currency freely. All cross-border wire transfers equal to or exceeding CAD 10,000 require a FINTRAC Electronic Funds Transfer Report, and physical cross-border currency movements equal to or exceeding CAD 10,000 require a Cross-Border Currency or Monetary Instruments Report.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to Low for pure foreign EMIs. Canadian law reserves deposit-taking for federally or provincially regulated banking entities. A foreign fintech operating as an MSB registered with FINTRAC (e.g., Wise) can clear low-value FX, but it cannot issue or confirm Commercial Letters of Credit for cotton bale exports. A full-service Tier 1 Canadian bank is mandatory for LC confirmation and documentary collection rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory, with limited remote exceptions. General partners and all authorised signatories must complete an in-person onboarding interview at a Canadian bank branch to satisfy standard AML/KYC policy. Remote video verification may be acceptable for individual limited partners, but the LP must produce a certified notarised partnership agreement, registered office address in Quebec, and maintain a board resolution authorising account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate ownership chart, legalised passports/IDs, tax identification numbers in each partner's residence country, independently sourced bank and asset statements proving the origin of contributed capital, and a formal source-of-wealth questionnaire.

Executory purchase and sale contracts, comprehensive packing lists, Bills of Lading, warehouse receipts, commodity inspection certificates (e.g., Cotton Incorporated or SGS), and proof of economic substance of the LP's brokerage operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-Border Wire Transfers to High-Risk Jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete CDD file on the ultimate beneficiary, underlying commercial invoices, shipping documents, and a negative news/sanctions screening report clearing all counterparties against the Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) and OSFI advisories.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must be routed via SWIFT MT103 over the Lynx/CHIPS network. The LP must classify injections as either non-resident partner capital contributions or intercompany shareholder loans, using ISO 20022 purpose codes such as 'C700' (payment for trade) or 'C001' (capital contribution) to satisfy correspondent bank due diligence. Incoming international wires over CAD 10,000 trigger a FINTRAC EFT Report.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for cotton inventory settlements shall use SWIFT MT103 open-account wire transfers, commercial Letters of Credit (Sight/Usance) for documentary transactions, and Documentary Collections (D/A or D/P). All disbursements must be accompanied by underlying trade invoices, with comprehensive FINTRAC record-keeping maintained for any batch exceeding CAD 10,000.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable Outright FX Forwards (CAD/USD; tenors matched to settlement date)
Note: NDFs are permissible only for non-convertible or illiquid currencies, not in ex-Canada CAD/USD where a deep spot market exists.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Quebec Legal Publicity Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of the date of initial registration of the limited partnership with REQ
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file within the prescribed window constitutes an offence under the Legal Publicity Act and may result in monetary penalties (up to C$2,000 for a legal person); after one year of continued default, REQ may strike the limited partnership from the register and terminate its juridical publicity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Partnership Information Return (T5013) and related schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a fiscal period ending December 31, filing is due no later than March 31 of the immediately following calendar year; for a non-calendar fiscal period, due within five months after the fiscal period end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted T5013 filings trigger a CRA penalty of C$25 per day per partner, with a minimum penalty of C$100 and a maximum of C$2,500 per partnership return; sustained non-filing may additionally lead to CRA prosecution and reallocation or denial of partnership losses.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Partnership Information Return and RL-31 information slips
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year partnership, return and RL-31 slips are due no later than March 31 of the following year; for a non-calendar fiscal period, due within five months after the fiscal period end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or failure to issue RL-31 slips exposes the limited partnership to Revenu Québec administrative penalties of C$25 per day per partner (minimum C$100, maximum C$2,500); provincial loss-sharing allocations may be denied until the return is filed.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory independent audit is mandatory for a Quebec limited partnership solely by reason of revenue or asset size. An audited annual engagement becomes compulsory only if required by the partnership agreement, by a lender or export-financing covenant, by the securities regulators if the LP is a public issuer, or by a specific partner resolution. Quebec does not impose an automatic audit obligation on non-public limited partnerships.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian private partnerships generally apply Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for annual financial statements supporting the T5013 and RL-31 returns; IFRS is required if the limited partnership is, or forms part of, a public reporting enterprise. The federal Income Tax Act also requires contemporaneous books and records maintained in Canadian dollars.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual REQ declaration confirms only the partnership's name, head office, general partner legal name and principal address, statutory activity code, and place of business. Limited partners and their beneficial holdings are not disclosed in the annual declaration. For AML/KYC compliance under Canadian federal legislation, the general partner must annually reconfirm full legal name, residential address, date of birth, citizenship, control percentage, and source of funds for each limited partner beneficially owning the partnership; this information is kept on a confidential internal record rather than filed with a public corporate register.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of limited partners and capital contributions (confidential; maintained by the general partner)
General partner's minute book and resolutions register
Register of annual declarations and government filings (REQ, CRA, and Revenu Québec correspondence)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% federal general corporate income tax rate after federal abatement; combined with Quebec provincial general corporate rate of 11.5%, the aggregate standard headline rate for a corporation with a permanent establishment in Quebec is 26.5%. The CA_LP limited partnership itself is fiscally transparent, so income is taxed at the partner level using the applicable federal and Quebec marginal rates.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No specific statutory tax holiday applies to international brokerage of ginned raw cotton or synthetic yarns. Preferential treatment includes the federal small business deduction for Canadian-controlled private corporate partners (effective federal rate as low as 9% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income), provincial small business deduction in Quebec (3.2% on the first CAD 500,000), capital cost allowance deductions, deductible arm's length expenses, and the general rate reduction for manufacturing and processing profits where applicable. The LP itself does not claim these incentives; eligibility is determined at the partner level.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 Partnership Information Return (federal, CRA) and RL-13 (Revenu Québec) filed for the limited partnership; electronic filing is mandatory for returns with over 100 T5013 slips; acceptable portals are CRA EFILE-approved software and Revenu Québec's e-Services for tax files.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Federal T5013 must be filed within five months after the partnership fiscal period end; Revenu Québec requires the provincial partnership information return within six months after fiscal period end. For a calendar-year 2025 fiscal period, federal due date is March 31, 2026 and provincial due date is June 30, 2026.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, mailing address, jurisdiction of formation, and provincial registration number of the limited partnership, together with the name and address of the general partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If no general partner is resident in Canada, provide the address of the designated Canadian agent or representative for service of notices and tax matters.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue, allowable expenses, net income or loss, and each partner's share of the result as determined by the partnership agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Canadian-source portion of partnership income allocated to a non-resident partner must be separately identified; treaty relief cannot be applied before computing the T5013 allocation without supporting NR301 declarations and Certificates of Residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: For each partner, the name, tax identification number, provincial and federal residency status, and percentage ownership of the limited partnership.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident limited partners must provide their home jurisdiction tax identification number and, where applicable, the Canada Revenue Agency non-resident account number; amounts allocated are reportable on a Canadian tax return where the income is effectively connected with a Canadian business.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file T5013 attracts a penalty of the greater of CAD 100 and CAD 10 per day for each day the return is late, up to CAD 2,500, under subsection 162(2.1) of the Income Tax Act; late Revenu Québec filings attract separate daily penalties plus interest, and repeated failures may trigger gross negligence penalties of up to 50% of misrepresented amounts.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal, CRA) and CO-17 (Revenu Québec) filed by each corporation that is a partner in the limited partnership; electronic filing is compulsory for all corporate income tax returns, using CRA EFILE or Revenu Québec electronic transmission portals.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T2 return must be filed no later than six months after the corporate partner's taxation year-end; the Quebec CO-17 must be filed no later than six months after the same fiscal year-end. Income tax balances are due no later than three months after year-end for Canadian-controlled private corporations and two months after year-end for other corporations; instalment timing rules apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The corporate partner's pro-rata share of the LP's business income or loss reported on T5013, adjusted for the tax basis in the partnership interest and any at-risk limitations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporate partner must include Canadian-source partnership income on a T2 return if the partnership carries on a business in Canada; the tax treaty residence article determines the right to tax and the applicable permanent establishment threshold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable income after deducting capital cost allowance, eligible capital expenditures, business investment losses, and any approved reserves for export receivables.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners are restricted in claiming deductions relating to expenses outside Canada unless incurred for the purpose of earning Canadian source business income; treaty non-discrimination clauses may protect branch deductions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal foreign tax credits, Quebec tax credits, investment tax credits, and dividend refunds; the LP's export income is generally active business income for small business deduction purposes if the corporate partner is a Canadian-controlled private corporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporate partner may only claim provincial tax credits if it has presence in Quebec; withholding taxes on dividends or deemed distributions are not creditable against Part I tax absent treaty or foreign tax credit mechanics.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late corporate filing penalty is 5% of unpaid tax balance plus 1% per full month of delay, capped at 12 months; failure to file by a non-resident foreign corporation additionally imposes an administrative penalty of CAD 1,500 to CAD 3,000 for each consecutive failure under subsection 162(2.2); gross negligence penalty is 50% of the amount incorrectly reported; recurring failures may yield director liability notices for unremitted source deductions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% statutory non-resident withholding tax on taxable dividends paid to non-residents under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act; rate is reduced by applicable tax treaties, including to 15% for portfolio dividends and 5% for qualifying substantial-holdings dividends under the Canada-US convention. Because the CA_LP is a limited partnership, ordinary profit distributions are not dividends and do not attract Part XIII withholding; only amounts characterizing as dividends out of a corporate partner or deemed dividends under section 212 are withheld.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident partner seeking treaty-based reduced withholding must complete and deliver CRA Form NR301 (Declaration of Eligibility for Benefits under a Tax Treaty), attach an up-to-date Certificate of Residence (TRC) from the jurisdiction of residence, provide the Canadian payer's name and account number, and, where necessary, file a T2 or T5013 return to claim a refund of excess withholding. For Quebec-specific source payments, the foreign recipient must also supply Revenu Québec with applicable schedule RL-18 or TP-1015 declarations to align provincial withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Federal statutory Part XIII rates: interest paid to non-residents is 25%, with an exemption for arm's length interest to unrelated lenders; royalties for the use of intellectual property are subject to 25% statutory withholding. Under the Canada-US tax treaty, qualifying arm's length interest is exempt from Canadian withholding, and industrial royalties are reduced to 10%; under many other Canadian DTAs the treaty royalty rate is 10% or less. Quebec's Taxation Act levies parallel provincial withholding on similar cross-border payments, but treaty caps apply to the combined federal-provincial burden, so the effective aggregate rate should be validated against the applicable DTA article.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation and T106 (International Non-Arm's-Length Transactions) reporting are mandatory when the aggregate fair market value of cross-border non-arm's-length transactions with non-residents exceeds CAD 1,000,000 in a taxation year; a separate Master File is not required under Canadian domestic law but the CRA expects comprehensive group-level analysis commensurate with OECD guidance.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not maintain offshore-model Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), but the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) under section 245, the common law sham doctrine, and Quebec Civil Code requirements for lawful exercise of civil rights deny tax benefits from artificial transactions lacking commercial substance. A Quebec limited partnership engaged exclusively in international cotton brokerage must maintain provincial registration, a Canadian place of business, real personnel, managed operations, and substantive decision-making in Canada to preserve treaty benefits and avoid re-characterization as a conduit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing export brokerage commissions, creating backdated invoices for raw cotton sales, understating partner allocations, or failing to report Canadian-source partnership income to CRA and Revenu Québec.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under section 239(1) of the Income Tax Act, a person who wilfully evades tax is guilty of an offence punishable by a fine of at least 50% and up to 200% of the tax attempted to evade, imprisonment for up to two years, or both; in addition, the civil gross negligence penalty under section 163(2) is 50% of the amount misreported, plus interest and arrears.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length prices for cotton brokering services that materially deviate from the CUP or TNMM benchmark, or failing to prepare and retain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation for the CAD 1,000,000 threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may re-determine taxable income under subsection 247(2); section 247(4) imposes a penalty equal to the greater of CAD 5,000 and 10% of the net adjustment amount arising from the transfer pricing mispricing; in egregious cases, misinformation penalties and gross negligence penalties may compound the exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Conduit and GAAR Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a tax-transparent Quebec limited partnership exclusively as a conduit to route cotton brokerage income to a low-tax or treaty-source jurisdiction without genuine business purpose, local administration, employees, or commercial risk.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR permits CRA to disregard the impugned transaction and re-attribute income to the economic owner; penalty equal to 50% of the resulting tax benefit applies if the transaction was motivated primarily by tax avoidance; in federal and Quebec civil procedures, courts may pierce the veil and treat the limited partnership as nonexistent for income tax purposes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Proceeds of Crime Act Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Handling cash or wire proceeds from cotton brokers through accounts that conceal beneficial ownership, failing to maintain a beneficial ownership register, or facilitating s trade-based money laundering through false invoicing in the cotton export chain.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, administrative monetary penalties can reach CAD 2,000,000 for an entity; criminal money laundering under the Criminal Code attracts imprisonment up to ten years; the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) may also impose compliance orders and freeze assets.
